This ZIP specifies compact block relay for the Zcash peer-to-peer network, adapted from BIP 152.

A compact block contains the block header, short identifiers for the block’s transactions, and its coinbase transaction; the receiver reconstructs the block from transactions it already has. Peers that both opt in may also relay a block before fully validating it, once its header and transaction commitments have been checked.

As in Bitcoin before BIP 152, a Zcash node announces a block only after fully validating it, and a peer that requests the block receives every transaction in it, although it has usually already received most of them through transaction relay. Both delay the propagation of new blocks between miners.

BIP 152 replaces transactions the receiver already has with short identifiers, and allows a block to be relayed before it is fully validated. It cannot be used in Zcash unchanged: Zcash block headers include an Equihash solution, and since NU5 a transaction’s txid does not commit to its authorizing data
, so short identifiers and the checks made before early relay need to cover the wtxid.
All messages defined in this ZIP are serialized in the standard encoding for P2P messages.

This ZIP differs from BIP 152 as follows:
The header is the Zcash block header, including the Equihash solution.
Short IDs are computed from the wtxid for v5 and later transactions, so version 1 of the encoding is not Bitcoin’s version 1.
Support is signalled by a service flag rather than a protocol version, and an unsupported version disables announcements rather than being negotiated.
The coinbase transaction is always prefilled, and all counts and sizes are bounded.
Early relay requires checking authorizing data, and is limited to children of the best tip.
Zebra and zcashd ignore unknown P2P messages after the handshake

, so a service flag is not needed to avoid disconnection. It is needed because both peers have to agree on the encoding, and on not penalizing authenticated blocks that fail later validation; an ignored message establishes neither. A protocol version signals support for a network upgrade, not for an optional relay policy.
The limit of 37,037 transactions is the 2,000,000-byte block size limit divided by 54 bytes, a lower bound on the size of a transaction.
Bit 16 avoids the service flags allocated in Zcash and Bitcoin
, the range 24 to 31 reserved for temporary experiments, and bits 12 to 14, which are used by pending Bitcoin proposals.

A short ID identifies a transaction only probabilistically. A node that skipped the checks in step 5 of [Receiving Compact Blocks] could accept a block whose authorizing data differs from the data committed to by its header.
An early relayed block can be invalid. Receiving one does not indicate that the block is valid, and nodes MUST fully validate it before accepting it.
